Action.description:
The action of a rule (#34).

Each action is an object with a `type`, and its options as optional
keys, so options can be added later without a breaking change.

oneOf.description: Permit execution.
Block execution.

allow_request.description:
The end user may raise an approval request (#11). Needs a
notification, and is not valid in a mandatory rule set.

kill_running.description:
Terminate already-running instances that match when the policy is
applied. Not valid for drivers or libraries.

on_unparseable.description:
Whether a version fact that is not a version counts towards the
rule applying (#32, #35). With `match`, each version criterion on
such a fact is taken in whichever direction makes the deny apply,
also under `not`. The rest of the tree is evaluated as usual.
`no_match`, the default, leaves the criterion `Unknown`, which
`unknown_as` then decides.

request_template.description: The approval request template to use. Only with `allow_request`.

unknown_as.description:
Whether the rule blocks when its match tree is `Unknown` because a
fact is missing or cannot be trusted (#32, #35). `no_match`, the
default, means an unknown fact does not block; `match` makes the
deny fail closed.

oneOf.description:
Record the match without changing the outcome. A non-terminal
annotation, used for detection and tagging.

Permit execution inside a containment profile (#14). The engine only
carries the reference.

profile_id.description: The containment profile the process runs under.

oneOf.description:
Permit execution with an elevated token (#12). The engine only
carries the directive.

auth.description: What the user must do to confirm.

reason_prompt.description:
If set, the user must give a reason, and this is the prompt shown:
one line of 1 to 256 characters, trimmed, with no control characters
(including tab and line breaks) and no bidirectional formatting
characters, so the prompt cannot be made to read differently.

token_profile.description: The access token profile to build the token from.

oneOf.description:
Mark the matching process as a trusted installer, updater or source
(#9, #114). This does not permit the process itself to run; an allow
rule decides that. The engine returns the directive.

scope_paths.description:
The folders whose new content becomes trusted: 1 to 32 absolute paths
(`C:\...`, `\\server\share\...`, or a known path variable such as
`%PROGRAMFILES%\...`), each at most 1024 bytes, written with `\`, and
unique (compared as the engine compares paths).

tag_output.description:
Tag the files written with a persistent trust claim, so they stay
trusted after the process exits. Off by default.

oneOf.description:
Skip the object entirely: no decision is logged. Only for performance
exclusions, never for executables or drivers, and validation always
warns.
No opinion. A first-match model continues with the next rule (#35).

anyOf.description: A string of at most 2048 bytes, with no control characters.

AllowTiebreak.description: Which allow decides among allows of different kinds.

oneOf.description:
`allow_contained`, then `allow`, then `allow_elevated` (with
`condition: always` before `if_required`). The default.

The reverse: `allow_elevated` (`if_required` before `always`), then
`allow`, then `allow_contained`.

ContainmentProfileRef.description: The ID of a containment profile (#14, #173).

ControlLevel.description: Whether a class of object is controlled.

oneOf.description: Not evaluated.
Evaluated, and would-block decisions are reported only.
Evaluated and enforced.

Criterion.description:
A test of one fact about the object or its context: `field operator
values`.

Values are combined with OR for positive operators and with AND for
negative ones (#32): `not_contains [a, b]` means neither `a` nor `b`.

case_sensitive.description:
Compare strings case-sensitively. Unset means the field's default
(#32), which is case-insensitive for every field defined so far.
Only text, paths, file names, account names and tags have a case;
other fields (hashes, versions, SIDs, group sets, yes-or-no facts and
session types) reject this option.

values.description:
1 to 25 values. Each is at most 2048 bytes of UTF-8; the schema can
only bound the length in characters, so validation checks the bytes.
`is_true` and `is_false` take no values, and the key may be left out.

Effects.description: The effect flags of one rule. Unset fields take the action's default.

help_url.description:
A link shown with the notification: an `https` URL of at most 2048
bytes. Only allowed when a notification is shown.

log.description:
Whether the decision produces a local event. `deny`, `audit`,
`allow_elevated` and `trust_source` need an event per decision, so
`summary` and `never` are not allowed on them.

notification_text.description:
The text of a `custom` notification: at most 2048 characters, with
the placeholders `{file}`, `{publisher}`, `{rule}`, `{user}` and
`{hash}`. Write `{{` and `}}` for literal braces. Required with
`notify: custom`, and only allowed with it.

notify.description: Whether the user is shown a notification.

severity.description: How serious the event is, for alerting (#16).

suppress_duplicates_secs.description:
The local de-duplication window, in seconds, at most 604800. `0`
turns de-duplication off. Detection counters still count every
occurrence.

tags.description:
Labels copied into the event, such as `lolbin` or
`mitre:T1218.005`: each 1 to 128 characters, at most 64.

upload.description: When the event is sent to the server.

ElevationAuth.description: The confirmation an `allow_elevated` action asks for.

oneOf.description: No confirmation. The default.
The user authenticates again.
The user completes a multi-factor challenge.
Every time the object runs.
Only when the object asks for administrator rights.

EnforcementOverride.description: How one rule relates to the policy mode (#36).

oneOf.description: Follow the effective mode. The default.
Enforce this rule even in audit or learning mode.
Never enforce this rule: it only reports what it would block.
Informational.
Low.
Medium.
High.
Critical.

Field.description:
The identity facts a criterion can test (#31).

This is the part of the #31 catalogue that has a matcher: hashes, the
signer, the path and the version resource. The other families (signer
constraints such as EKU and TBS hashes, packaged apps, installers,
ownership, origin and process relationships) arrive in later minor
versions, each with its facts and matcher.

oneOf.description: SHA-256 of the whole file. The primary identity (ADR 0008).
SHA-384 of the whole file.
SHA-512 of the whole file.

SHA-256 Authenticode image hash: the PE image without its checksum,
security directory entry and certificate table.
SHA-1 Authenticode image hash. Compatibility only (ADR 0008).

SHA-256 hash of the first page of the image, for OS-native policy
formats. It covers only that page, so it is a weak identity alone.

SHA-1 hash of the first page of the image. Compatibility only
(ADR 0008).

SHA-256 of an installer package with its timestamps left out, so
rebuilds of the same content share one value (#3).
SHA-1 of the whole file. Compatibility only (ADR 0008).
MD5 of the whole file. Compatibility only (ADR 0008).
The leaf signer's subject common name.
The common name of the leaf certificate's issuer.
The SHA-256 thumbprint of the leaf certificate.
The normalised full path.
The parent directory.
The on-disk file name.
The file extension, without its leading dot.
The original file name from the version resource.
The internal name from the version resource.
The file description from the version resource.
The product name from the version resource.
The company name from the version resource.
The file version from the version resource.
The product version from the version resource.
Context (#33): the SID of the user the process runs as.

Context (#33): the user's account name, as `DOMAIN\user` or as a
user principal name (`user@example.org`). Either form can match.
Regular expressions are not allowed: match principals by SID where
you can (#32).

Context (#33): the groups in the user's token, as SIDs, and the
user's cloud-directory groups, as object IDs.
Context (#33): the SID of the user's primary group.

Context (#33): the token holds the local Administrators group,
enabled or filtered by UAC.
Context (#33): the token is elevated.
Context (#33): the user is a service account.
Context (#33): the user is the local system account.
Context (#33): the device's host name.
Context (#33): the device's fully qualified domain name.
Context (#33): the DNS name of the device's domain.
Context (#33): the device's NetBIOS name.
Context (#33): the directory site the device is in.

Context (#33): the device's computer groups, as SIDs, and its
cloud-directory device groups, as object IDs.
Context (#33): the Palisade tags assigned to the device.
Context (#33): the operating system version.
Context (#33): the operating system edition.
Context (#33): the processor architecture, such as `x64` or `arm64`.
Context (#33): the device runs a server edition.
Context (#33): the device is a domain controller.
Context (#33): the device is a laptop.
Context (#33): the device is a virtual desktop.
Context (#33): the device is a multi-session terminal server.

Context (#33): how the session was started: `console`, `rdp`,
`remote_shell`, `service`, `batch` or `network`.

Context (#33): the host name of the client connected to the session,
on a multi-session host.
Context (#33): the session is remote.

LogLevel.description: Whether a decision produces a local event.

oneOf.description: Every decision produces an event.

Decisions are aggregated into periodic summaries per device, user,
object and rule. The default for allow rules.
A sample of decisions produces events.
No event.

Match.description:
A condition tree (#33).

Each node is an object with exactly one key: `all`, `any`, `not` or
`criterion`.

oneOf.description: Matches when every child matches. Needs at least one child.
Matches when any child matches. Needs at least one child.
Matches when the child does not.
One test of one fact.

Metadata.description: Governance metadata (#40). More fields arrive with #40.

tags.description: Free-form labels, each 1 to 128 characters, at most 64.

Mode.description:
How a policy's decisions take effect (#36).

The variants are declared from weakest to strongest, so the derived
ordering ranks them. The "strictest" merge in #36 treats `learning` and
`audit` as equally strong; that rule belongs to the merge code, not to this
ordering.

oneOf.description: The engine is not consulted. The device is reported as unprotected.
Evaluate fully, allow everything, and report would-block decisions.
Like `monitor`, with a full event for every decision.
Audit, and report every would-block object as a learning candidate.
Decisions take effect: blocked means blocked.

ModeOptions.description: Mode settings besides the base `mode`. Each is optional in a document.

disconnected_after_secs.description:
How long after its last successful check-in a device counts as
disconnected, in seconds: 60 to 2592000, and at least the check-in
interval. Unset means three check-in intervals.

mode_by_type.description:
The mode per object type, replacing the base mode for that type:
for example `script.powershell: audit` while everything else is
enforced. `disabled` is not allowed here: only a whole device can
be disabled.

mode_disconnected.description:
The base mode while the device is disconnected: `mode` itself or a
stricter mode, so losing the server never relaxes a device. It also
raises a weaker `mode_by_type`. Unset means the same as `mode`.

Notify.description: Whether the user is shown a notification (#11).

oneOf.description: No notification.
The policy's default notification.
The rule's `notification_text`.

ObjectType.description: The class of object being evaluated. Scripts are `script.<kind>`.

Operator.description:
How a criterion compares the fact with its values (#32). Positive
operators match if any value matches; negative operators (`not_*`)
match if no value does, and never match a fact that is unknown.

oneOf.description: Equal to any value.
Equal to none of the values.

Starts with any value. On paths, the value must end at a component
boundary: `C:\Tools` does not match `C:\ToolsX`.
Ends with any value.
Contains any value.
Contains none of the values.
Matches any wildcard pattern.
Matches none of the wildcard patterns.

Matches any regular expression. Anchored at both ends, and run by a
linear-time engine without look-around or backreferences.
Matches none of the regular expressions.
Version equal to any value.
Version greater than the value.
Version greater than or equal to the value.
Version less than the value.
Version less than or equal to the value.

Version within `[min, max]`, both inclusive. Takes exactly two
values, the minimum first.
The set holds any of the values (#33).
The set holds none of the values (#33).
The fact is true. Takes no values (#33).

The fact is false. Takes no values (#33). On an unknown fact it is
unknown, like every other test.

Os.description:
The operating system a rule set targets. Other systems are reserved and
will be added in a minor version.

oneOf.description: Windows.

Policy.description: The decision part of a policy: which rule sets apply, and how.

id.description: Stable ID. Renaming the policy never changes it.

mode.description:
The base enforcement mode (#36). `disabled` is not allowed: only a
device can be disabled, with a reason and an expiry.

mode_options.description: The modes per object type and while disconnected (#36).

name.description:
Display name: 1 to 128 characters, trimmed, no control characters.
Uniqueness within a tenant is checked by the server (#10).

precedence_model.description: How matching rules are combined (#35, ADR 0004).

precedence_options.description:
Settings of the precedence models (#35). An option the selected
model does not use is ignored, with a warning.

revision.description: Monotonic revision, raised by the server on every change (#10).

rule_sets.description: The rule sets that apply, in order, by ID.

settings.description: Typed settings. Every field has a documented default.

PolicyId.description: The stable ID of a policy.

PolicySettings.description:
Settings that apply to the whole policy. Every field is optional in a
document and has the default shown in the schema.

advanced.description:
Engineering settings, checked against a registry of known keys. The
registry is empty in this version, so any key is rejected unless
`allow_unknown_advanced` is set.

allow_unknown_advanced.description: Accept keys in `advanced` that the registry does not know.

capture_command_line.description:
Whether the agent records process command lines. Off by default for
privacy (#18).

decision_cache_ttl_secs.description: How long a decision may be cached, in seconds. `0` disables the cache.

max_ancestor_depth.description: How many ancestors process criteria may inspect (#31).

override_durations.description:
Durations, in minutes, offered for override sessions (#9). At most 5
slots, each at most 10080. `0` marks a disabled slot.

script_control.description: Control level for scripts of a kind not listed in `script_control_by_kind`.

script_control_by_kind.description: Control level per script kind, overriding `script_control`.

PrecedenceModel.description:
How the matching rules of the ordinary rule sets are combined (#35).

The mandatory-deny tier and the implicit deny for unmatched files apply
under every model (ADR 0004). The semantics of each model are in
[`crate::precedence`].

oneOf.description: Any matching deny blocks; otherwise any matching allow allows. The default.
Any matching allow allows. Not recommended for Essential Eight.
The rule with the most specific identity wins.
Rules are ordered, and the first match decides.
The rule with the winning numeric priority decides.

PrecedenceOptions.description: Settings of the precedence models. Each is optional in a document.

allow_tiebreak.description:
Which allow decides when several allow rules of different kinds
could (`deny_wins`, `allow_wins` and `specificity`). The default,
`most_restrictive`, ranks `allow_contained` over `allow` over
`allow_elevated`.

curated_first.description:
`first_match` only: rules of curated (read-only) rule sets are
evaluated before every custom rule, whatever their `order`. On by
default.

granularity_tiebreak.description:
`allow_wins` only: within one rule set, a rule with a more specific
identity beats a less specific one before allow-over-deny applies,
so a denied file in an allowed folder stays denied. Off by default.

priority_direction.description:
`priority` only: whether the lowest or the highest `priority`
number wins. `lower_wins` by default.

same_tier_tiebreak.description:
`specificity` only: which action wins between rules of the same
specificity. `deny` by default.

oneOf.description: The lowest number wins. The default.
The highest number wins.

RequestTemplateRef.description: The ID of an approval request template (#11).

Rule.description: One rule: a match tree and the action taken when it matches.

display_id.description: Human short ID from the tenant's sequence, `R-` and 6 to 12 digits.

effects.description:
Logging, upload, notification, severity and tags (#34). Unset
fields take the action's defaults.

enabled.description: Disabled rules are kept, but never decide.

enforcement_override.description: Per-rule enforcement override (#36). Only for `deny` rules.

name.description: Display name, with the same rules as a policy name.

object_types.description: The object classes the rule applies to. Empty means every class.

order.description:
Position for the `first_match` model (#35): 0 to 1000000, lowest
first. Rules of custom (not read-only) rule sets use 100001 to
999989; the other ranges are reserved for system, curated and
catch-all rules.

RuleId.description: The stable ID of a rule. It is never reused, even after the rule is deleted.

RuleSet.description: A named, reusable, ordered collection of rules.

kind.description: What the rule set is for.

mandatory.description:
Only for `blocklist`: evaluated in the non-overridable mandatory-deny
tier (#35, ADR 0004).

mode_override.description:
Only for a blocklist that is not mandatory: the mode its rules
decide in, replacing the mode for the object's type, for example to
try a new blocklist in `audit` (#36). `disabled` is not allowed.

name.description: Display name, with the same rules as a policy name.

os.description: The operating system the rules are written for.

read_only.description: Curated sets are read-only: edit a duplicate instead.

version.description: The content version of this rule set, for display (for example `3.0`).

RuleSetId.description: The stable ID of a rule set.

RuleSetKind.description: The purpose of a rule set.

oneOf.description: Rules that allow.
Rules that deny.
A baseline of what was present at a point in time.
Trusted sources (#9).
Elevation rules (#12).
Containment rules (#14).
Any mix of actions.

SchemaVersion.description: A semantic version MAJOR.MINOR.PATCH, without pre-release or build suffixes.

TierTiebreak.description: Which action wins between rules of the same specificity.

oneOf.description: A deny beats an allow. The default.
An allow beats a deny.

TimeZoneBasis.description: The clock that schedules are interpreted in.

oneOf.description: The device's local time zone.
Coordinated Universal Time.

TokenProfileRef.description: The ID of an access token profile for elevation (#12, #150).

TrustMode.description: How far trust from a `trust_source` action reaches (#114).

oneOf.description: Only files the designated process writes itself.
Files the designated process and all its descendants write.

UnknownAs.description: How a deny rule treats a result it cannot decide (#32, #35).

oneOf.description: The rule does not apply. The default.
The rule applies, so the deny blocks.

Upload.description: When an event is sent to the server.

oneOf.description: As soon as possible.
With the next batch.
Never: kept in the local log only.

Uuid7.description: A UUID version 7 in canonical lowercase form.

description: A versioned policy document: one policy and the rule sets it uses.

rule_sets.description:
The rule sets the policy references, in any order. The policy's
`rule_sets` list gives the order that applies.

schema_version.description:
The version of this schema the document was written for. A reader
accepts the same major version and any minor version.
